onboardingStep1Body: A high-visibility Material 3 geological compass-clinometer designed for rapid, accurate Strike and Dip measurements in the field.
onboardingStep2Body:
• Planar Mode: Place the back of your phone flat on a bedding plane to capture Strike & Dip simultaneously.
• Edge Mode: Align the long edge of the phone just like a classic clinometer.
onboardingStep3Body: Measuring overhead or hard-to-see outcrops? Press the physical Volume Keys (+/-) to lock readings with haptic & voice feedback. You can also zero-out camera bump tilt.
onboardingStep4Body: Compute true-north magnetic declination automatically from your GPS coordinates (WMM) and choose your preferred compass dial style.
helpPageSubtitle: Field procedures for measuring Strike & Dip and feature reference
helpStep1Desc: Planar Mode (Back Flat) is recommended for fast, simultaneous Strike & Dip measurement by placing the back of the phone on the bedding plane.
helpStep2Desc: Choose a smooth surface on the rock layer and wait briefly for the compass & spirit level to settle.
helpStep3Desc: Even on overhead overhangs where you cannot see the screen, press Volume Up/Down to lock the reading with haptic & voice feedback.
helpStep4Desc: Tap 'Log Data' to save the measurement with outcrop ID, notes, and GPS coordinates. Export all records as CSV anytime.
helpSurfaceModeIntro: Place the back of your phone flat against the bedding plane. The 3-axis accelerometer and magnetometer compute the Strike line and maximum Dip simultaneously.
helpDiagramPoint1Title: Phone Orientation: Portrait, Landscape, or Diagonal all give identical results
helpDiagramPoint1Desc: Because Kayo-Clino computes Strike & Dip directly from the 3D surface normal vector of the phone's back, rotating the phone on the bedding plane does not affect the reading.
helpDiagramPoint2Title: Most Important: Keep the back flush against the rock surface
helpDiagramPoint2Desc: Any gap between the phone back and the rock introduces tilt error. Use a field notebook or clipboard on rough outcrops, or use Camera Bump Zero-Calibration.
helpDiagramPoint3Title: Tip: Hold at whatever angle is easiest to read or reach
helpDiagramPoint3Desc: Hold the phone comfortably. For overhead or blind surfaces, press a physical Volume Key to HOLD the reading, then bring the phone down to inspect it.
helpEdgeModeIntro: Works like a traditional analog clinometer: align the long side of the phone horizontally with the rock face to measure Strike, then align down-slope to measure Dip angle.
helpNotation1Desc: Expresses Strike as degrees East or West from North (e.g., N 30° E), paired with Dip angle and quadrant direction (e.g., 45° SE).
helpNotation2Desc: International standard (000°–359°). Point your right thumb along the Strike azimuth so your fingers point down-dip.
helpNotation3Desc: Pairs the Dip angle (0°–90°) with the steepest down-slope azimuth (000°–359°). Ideal for 3D structural modeling.
helpSec4Title: 4. Why Are E and W Swapped on the Dial?
helpSec4Body:
Unlike a standard hiking compass, geological clinometers swap East (E) and West (W) on the bezel.

When you point the top of the instrument along the Strike direction, the magnetic needle points directly to the correct quadrant angle (N○○°E or N○○°W) on the scale.

Use the 'E/W Swap' button in the top bar to switch between a Clinometer Dial and a Standard Compass anytime.
helpFeat1Title: Volume Key HOLD & Accessibility Voice Readout (TTS)
helpFeat1Desc: Lock measurements one-handed using Volume Up/Down. Enable Voice Readout in Settings to hear Strike & Dip spoken aloud upon locking.
helpFeat2Desc: Automatically compute local magnetic declination from GPS coordinates using the World Magnetic Model (WMM), or pick a regional preset.
helpFeat3Desc: Place your phone on a flat table and tap 'Calibrate Flat Surface (0°)' in Settings to cancel out rear camera bump tilt.
helpFeat4Desc: Test Strike and Dip behavior indoors or in classrooms using manual sliders.
helpWebCardDesc: Learn more about geological compass-clinometers and Strike & Dip measurement on Wikipedia and the Geological Survey of Japan (GSJ).

whatIsKayoBtn: 🌺 What is "Kayo"? (Geology of the Kayo Formation)
whatIsKayoTitle: 🌺 What is "Kayo"? — The Kayo Formation & Folds
whatIsKayoSubtitle: Eocene Shimanto-Belt Equivalent Turbidites & Accretionary Prism Tectonics
whatIsKayoSec1Body: Named after the Eocene Kayo Formation (~40 Ma) exposed along the Kayo and Sokoniya coast of Nago City in northern Okinawa Island (Kunigami Belt), 'Kayo-Clino' pays tribute to one of Japan's premier structural geology sites. Structurally correlated with the Shimanto Belt accretionary complex of southwest Japan, the formation comprises trench-fill flysch—sandstone-dominant turbidites alternating rhythmically with mudstone. Primary sedimentary structures such as Bouma sequences (graded bedding) and sole markings (flute casts and load casts) are well preserved on bed bases, providing critical kinematic indicators for paleocurrent reconstruction and stratigraphic way-up determination.
whatIsKayoSec2Body:
Designated a National Natural Monument of Japan ('Folds of the Kayo Formation'), the strata exhibit intense deformation formed via offscraping, duplex underplating, and thrust faulting within a subduction-zone accretionary prism, superimposed on early-diagenetic submarine slump structures.
Outcrops display textbook examples of sharp-hinged chevron (kink) folds, recumbent and isoclinal folds with sub-horizontal axial planes, and completely overturned strata.
Because bedding strike, dip angle, and stratigraphic polarity invert rapidly over decimeter-to-meter scales across fold hinges and thrust sheets, systematic clinometer measurements are indispensable for structural analysis.
whatIsKayoSec3Body: The type-locality outcrops around Kayo Beach and Cape Ban are situated on a coastal wave-cut bench within the intertidal zone and are submerged at high tide. Field geologists planning structural measurements should consult local tide tables and schedule traverses during spring low tide.
